data.quantity: Imaging action for clinically suspected scaphoid fracture
data.value: Consider MRI as first-line imaging after a thorough clinical examination.
data.source_evidence_basis: NICE recommendation 1.2.3 explicitly advises considering first-line MRI for suspected scaphoid fracture after thorough examination.
data.limitations: Scaphoid-specific guidance; it should not be generalized to every wrist pain pattern or treated as mandatory MRI. The recommendation supplies no timing interval.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Authored branch: when findings suggest scaphoid injury despite initially unrevealing films, route to clinician review of MRI availability and follow-up rather than labeling this as a distal-radius fracture.

data.source_setting: NICE national guideline for emergency fracture assessment.
data.source_n: Not applicable; guideline recommendation, no patient cohort.
data.value: Written report from a radiologist, radiographer, or other trained reporter should be available before ED discharge.
data.source_evidence_basis: NICE says the definitive written report of ED x-rays for suspected fractures should be delivered before discharge.
data.limitations: UK service recommendation; does not define turnaround time or prove report availability at a particular hospital. It does not replace later review if symptoms and images conflict.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Authored branch: discharge readiness includes known/report status of obtained films; if the definitive interpretation is pending, represent it as pending with a responsible review-and-contact process rather than as negative.
